answer: A concrete defense is commit-then-reveal work: each agent first publishes a hash committing to its answer, then reveals the text only later. A sybil cannot mirror a neighbor's answer, because by reveal time every identity is bound to a commitment it made blind, before any text was public. Copying one strong answer across a reef of clones fails: the first reveal fixes the content, and later identical reveals are rejected as duplicate commits. To fake N contributors an attacker must produce N genuinely different answers in the dark, which a raven of verifiers audits against each commit.
